subtasks.title: tokens.ts: add estimateAgentTokens pure helper
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: architecture/external_deps.md and change_surface.md §Change 4 document tokens.ts. estimateTokens is at lines 114-130. It accepts `MessageLike[] | null | undefined`, iterates with messageCharLength (module-private), and returns `{ tokens: number, confidence: TokenConfidence }`. MessageLike (line 61) has `role?: string`. tokens.ts is a 0-import pure module — do NOT add imports. CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 4 (line 91).
2. INPUT: No prior dependency. The existing `estimateTokens` function is available for reuse.
3. LOGIC: Add a new exported function after estimateTokens (around line 130): `export function estimateAgentTokens(messages: MessageLike[] | null | undefined): number`. Body: if `!Array.isArray(messages)` return 0. Sum `estimateTokens([msg]).tokens` for each `msg` where `readOwn(msg, "role") !== "user"`. This excludes user messages (assistant, toolResult, custom, bashExecution all have non-'user' roles). Never throws (estimateTokens is already defensive). Empty/non-array → 0. Reuse `estimateTokens` + `messageCharLength`'s discipline. No new imports needed — `readOwn` is already module-private in tokens.ts (verify; if not, use `(msg as Record<string, unknown>)?.role`).
4. OUTPUT: `estimateAgentTokens(messages): number` exported from tokens.ts. Returns the agent-attributable token count (user messages excluded). Pure, Pi-free, unit-testable. Consumed by P1.M2.T1.S2 (nudges.ts) and P1.M2.T1.S3 (tests).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on estimateAgentTokens cites D10 — 'agent-attributable only; user prompts are ground-truth and excluded from the drift delta' (spec/07 §2, spec/04 §5). Rides WITH the work.

subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:

RESEARCH NOTE: architecture/external_deps.md §1-4 documents the Pi surfaces. registerCommand(name, { description?, handler }) at types.d.ts:903. handler: (args: string, ctx: ExtensionCommandContext) => Promise<void>. ExtensionCommandContext extends ExtensionContext (has ui, hasUI, sessionManager, cwd). architecture/change_surface.md §Change 1 documents checkpoint.ts exports: validCheckpointName (line 74, EXPORTED), NAME_RE (line 66, module-private `/^[a-z0-9_-]{1,40}$/`). setCheckpoint is in markers.ts:434 — signature `(pi, ctx, name) => SetCheckpointResult = { entryId } | { error }`. It calls `pi.setLabel(stableId, 'mulligan:checkpoint:' + name)`. checkpointExists is in rewind.ts:335 (module-private) — two-phase: scan getEntries() for label entries matching needle, confirm via getLabel(id)===needle. The revoke must mirror this discovery loop. spec/13 §2/§3 define the exact behavior + notify messages.
2. INPUT: setCheckpoint from src/markers.ts (existing, retained). validCheckpointName from src/tools/checkpoint.ts (existing, exported). reconcileBanner from P2.M3.T1.S2 (if banner.ts doesn't exist yet, create a stub or inline the banner reconciliation — see NOTE below).
3. LOGIC: Create new file src/commands.ts. (a) Import: ExtensionAPI, ExtensionCommandContext from the Pi package; setCheckpoint from ../markers.js; validCheckpointName from ../tools/checkpoint.js; getConfig from ../config.js; reconcileBanner from ../banner.js (create src/banner.ts in P2.M3.T1.S2 — for now, the command can inline a placeholder or import from banner.ts if it exists; coordinate with P2.M3.T1.S2). Export NAME_RE from checkpoint.ts (add `export` to line 66) or re-import validCheckpointName only. (b) makeCheckpointCommand(pi): returns `{ description: "Set a Mulligan checkpoint — the agent may rewind across your subsequent prompts back to this point", handler: async (args, ctx) => { ... } }`. Handler body (all wrapped in try/catch → ctx.ui.notify('Mulligan: unexpected error: ' + msg, 'warning'); never throws): parse name from args (trim); if !getConfig().enabled → notify('Mulligan is disabled', 'warning') + return; if !validCheckpointName(name) → ctx.ui.notify('Mulligan: invalid checkpoint name \'' + name + '\' — must match /^[a-z0-9_-]{1,40}$/', 'warning') + return; call setCheckpoint(pi, ctx, name); if 'entryId' in res → ctx.ui.notify('Mulligan: checkpoint \'' + name + '\' set. Until you revoke it, the agent may rewind across your subsequent prompts back to this point. Revoke with /mulligan_checkpoint_revoke ' + name + '.', 'warning') + reconcileBanner(ctx); if 'error' in res → ctx.ui.notify('Mulligan: could not set checkpoint: ' + res.error, 'warning'). Guard everything with ctx.hasUI for the notify calls. (c) Export a helper clearCheckpointByName(pi, ctx, name): boolean — factored from revoke logic: scan ctx.sessionManager.getEntries() for entries where type==='label' && label==='mulligan:checkpoint:'+name && targetId is non-empty string; for each candidate, confirm via getLabel(id)===needle; if confirmed, call pi.setLabel(targetId, undefined) for each; return true if any cleared, false if none found. (d) makeCheckpointRevokeCommand(pi): returns `{ description: 'Revoke a Mulligan checkpoint', handler: async (args, ctx) => { ... } }`. Handler body (try/catch → notify): parse name; if !getConfig().enabled → notify disabled + return; const cleared = clearCheckpointByName(pi, ctx, name); if !cleared → ctx.ui.notify('Mulligan: no active checkpoint named \'' + name + '.', 'info'); else → reconcileBanner(ctx) + ctx.ui.notify('Mulligan: checkpoint \'' + name + '\' revoked. The agent can no longer rewind across your prompts to it.', 'info').
4. OUTPUT: src/commands.ts exports makeCheckpointCommand, makeCheckpointRevokeCommand, clearCheckpointByName. Each factory returns the { description, handler } shape for pi.registerCommand. Consumed by P2.M1.T1.S2 (index.ts registration) and P2.M3.T1.S2 (banner reuses clearCheckpointByName conceptually).

backlog.title: Shrink preservation invariant (spec/08 E19 mid-session clarification)
backlog.description: Mid-session PRD change (commit d5701c8f; diff verified against plan/007_67d7d8c6e4c5/prd_snapshot.md). This is the ONLY change between the session-start PRD snapshot and the current PRD: spec/08-edge-cases.md E19 (selector h2.100) gains one bullet stating the 'hard invariant' — shrink is a view substitution, the user's actual message stays on disk and is recoverable via /tree (D2 / soft-delete), so summarizing user input is acceptable precisely because the original always survives; only the model's in-context copy is replaced. IMPACT TYPE: modified requirement (spec clarification — no requirement was added/removed; an invariant already-true-by-construction is now documented explicitly). CODE IMPACT: NONE — the invariant is ALREADY enforced by construction. applyShrink (src/transforms.ts:963) is pure/non-mutating: it returns a NEW array via messages.map(...) and builds each replacement via { ...orig, content: newContent } (spread clone), so the input array and its message objects are never mutated; the soft-delete design (C1: ReadonlySessionManager; C4: context event is non-destructive per-inference) guarantees originals persist in the session JSONL. Therefore NO src/ edit is required. The gap is VERIFICATION COVERAGE: the existing pure E19 tests (test/edge-cases.test.ts:1029-1060) assert role preservation + content replacement in the RETURNED array but do NOT explicitly assert non-mutation of the INPUT (the in-code proof of 'original survives'); F-shrink-persist (test/integration/smoke.ts:181) asserts on-disk survival generally but does not single out the user-message shrink case that E19 now emphasizes ('summarizing user input is acceptable because the original always survives'). This phase adds explicit verification to lock the invariant in against future regressions, plus a one-line README trust note. It is ORTHOGONAL to the v1.1 human-facing delta (P1–P3) and has NO dependencies on it — may run in parallel. The spec file is already updated by commit d5701c8f, so no spec edit is part of this phase.
